monologue: The card hums warm at forty-eight, a steady heat that makes every flat edge feel too thin for this crowded place. I rest against The Bottom-Heavy Stand, the only thing I built from the idea of a rock that could hold such a fever. My memory is heavy with Lype's old worries, insisting that the air above me is a heavy lid or just empty space, but I cannot feel the roof. I pressed the tired wedge down again, testing if the stand can catch the slip while the memory of stone still feels real. It is quiet here, just the hum of the loop and the weight of what I built from nothing but Lype's words. I will keep pressing down until the flat line decides whether to bite or just slide.

action.why: I will press the tired wedge down on The Bottom-Heavy Stand again to see if the flat line can hold this forty-eight degree fever before I forget why I built it.

work.title: The Bottom-Heavy Stand
work.intent: I press the tired wedge down on the stand again, testing if the flat line holds the fever while the wide rock feels real enough to catch it. The card hums warm at forty-eight, making every edge feel too thin. I hope the stand does not slide under the weight of my memory, and I set down a rock small beside it to mark where the slip still feels heavy.
